title: Quick Revision: Combustion and Flame

bullets: **Combustion** is a chemical process in which a substance reacts with oxygen to give off heat (and often light).
Three things are needed: **fuel, air (oxygen), and heating to the ignition temperature**. Remove any one and the fire goes out.
**Ignition temperature:** the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire. Inflammable substances (petrol, LPG, alcohol) have very low ignition temperatures.

bullets: Water cools the fuel below its ignition temperature, but must **not** be used on electrical fires or oil and petrol fires.
**Carbon dioxide** is the best extinguisher for electrical and oil fires: it is heavier than oxygen, so it covers the fire like a blanket, and it also cools it.
A good fuel is cheap, easily available, burns at a moderate rate, has a high calorific value and leaves little residue.
Calorific value (kJ/kg): hydrogen about 1,50,000 · LPG about 55,000 · petrol and kerosene about 45,000 · coal 25,000–33,000 · wood 17,000–22,000 · cow dung cake 6,000–8,000.
Harmful effects: carbon monoxide is poisonous; more CO_{2} adds to global warming; oxides of sulphur and nitrogen cause acid rain.
